subject: On-prem bundle: platform fee vs usage discount — clarifying ops credits
messages:
From: Rafael Gonzales <rafael.gonzales@edgewave.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: EdgeWave Systems Procurement <procurement@edgewave.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Looking for clarity on on-prem commercial tradeoffs

Hi Olga —

Thanks again for the rundown in last week's demo. Procurement asked me to get a clearer picture on how Redwood is thinking about the economics for the on-prem (VPC) bundle. Two specific asks from our side:

1) Can we trade down the platform (annual) fee if we lock to a higher usage commitment? For us, a large up-front platform fee is a budgeting headache.
2) We need a short-term ops/implementation credit while we run migration and pilot in Q3 — ideally something that offsets professional services and early engineering hours.

I've attached EdgeWave's RFP so you have the context (we referenced section 4.2). High level: 3yr deploy, initial pilot ~6 months, expected token volumes ramping to 2B tokens/month by year 2.

Can you share a couple alternative commercial approaches (platform fee lower + usage uplift vs current platform fee + no uplift) and what concessions/resources Redwood would provide (onboarding hours, SLA credits, training)?

Best,
Rafael
Principal Product Manager
EdgeWave Systems

Attachments: EdgeWave_RFP.pdf (attached)

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Gonzales <rafael.gonzales@edgewave.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Looking for clarity on on-prem commercial tradeoffs

Hi Rafael —

Thanks for the RFP and the clear asks. I pulled together two alternative sketches and attached the pricing matrix (redwood_onprem_pricing_matrix.xlsx). Highlights up front:

Option A — Lower platform fee + higher committed usage
- Platform fee: $250k/year (instead of standard $500k)
- Commit: 1.5B tokens/month year 1, 2B tokens/month thereafter
- Includes: 200 onboarding hours, dedicated CS technical lead for pilot, standard SLA (99.9%)

Option B — Standard platform fee + smaller commit
- Platform fee: $500k/year
- Commit: 1.0B tokens/month year 1, 1.5B tokens/month thereafter
- Includes: 350 onboarding hours, prioritized engineering support during migration, 30k USD one-time implementation credit

On the ops credit: we can structure a timebound credit tied to specific milestones (pilot signoff, production go-live). Typical form: a $75k implementation credit applied against the SOW / invoice schedule, or 150 engineering hours dedicated to the migration.

If you think a blended approach works (lower platform fee + modest ops credit), we can propose that to procurement. Marissa has the final pricing approval for non-standard credits — looping her in.

Quick Q for procurement: do you want the ops credit as a dollar credit (applied to invoice) or as time-limited engineering hours? Some customers prefer hours to avoid accounting complications.

Cheers,
Olga Petrov
Strategic Accounts — On-prem Deployments
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_onprem_pricing_matrix.xlsx (attached)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Gonzales <rafael.gonzales@edgewave.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2027 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: On-prem bundle: pricing matrix + recommended concession structure

Rafael / Olga — forwarding the matrix with recommended fallbacks. Key negotiation plays (from commercial):

- If EdgeWave signs a 3yr deal with the high-volume ramp profile, we can:
  * Reduce platform fee to $200k/year in Year 1 (and $300k thereafter)
  * Guarantee a blended token price floor that saves ~18% vs list over the committed volume
  * Provide a one-time onboarding credit: either $100k invoice credit or 200 engineering hours valid for 9 months

- If you prefer to avoid a large platform fee, we can alternatively offer no platform fee for Year 1 but with a higher per-token floor and an escalator clause — this is operationally riskier for Redwood and would require a usage ramp cadence.

I'll put the formal commercial language in the term sheet once we confirm which direction you prefer. Rafael — which structure do you want us to model into a draft SOW?

Thanks,
Marissa

Thanks Marissa — helpful framing. A few follow-ups from procurement: 

1) Platform fee swap: EdgeWave's preference is to reduce the platform fee materially in Year 1 (ideally to $0–$100k) in exchange for a higher committed token floor and a modest uplift in per-token price for overages during Year 1. Can you model a $0 platform fee for Year 1 + commit to 1.25B tokens/month with an overage premium of 8%?

2) Ops/implementation credit: We prefer engineering hours (to manage accounting) — target 180 hours, usable in the pilot + 3 months of go-live support.

3) SLA: We need a clear escalation path for the pilot phase (3 months) with on-call windows and a named on-call engineer.

Would Redwood accept (1) $0 platform fee Yr1, (2) 1.25B commit/mth Yr1, (3) 180 engineering hours credit, and (4) pilot escalation SLA with named engineer? If you can agree in principle, we can prepare a PO contingent on the final SOW and appendix.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — procurement is on a tight cadence for vendor selection.

— Rafael

Subject: Internal: EdgeWave ask — $0 platform fee Yr1 + 180 hours credit — need approval

Marissa / Sean —

Summarizing EdgeWave's ask from procurement (see thread):
- $0 platform fee Year 1
- Commit: 1.25B tokens/month Year 1 (ramp to 2B by Year 2)
- 180 engineering hours as a migration/pilot credit, valid pilot → +90 days
- Named on-call engineer during pilot window (3 months)

Commercial impact (rough): if accepted, Year 1 net revenue drops ~40% vs standard platform fee scenario, but we gain a 3yr committed relationship with sizeable token volume. Risk to Redwood: heavy early support without platform anchoring.

Recommended counter (commercial + ops balanced):
1) Approve $50k platform fee Year 1 (instead of $0) to cover minimal platform stewardship.
2) Approve 120 engineering hours credit (we can convert additional hours to discounted hourly T&M post-pilot).
3) Named on-call engineer during pilot (RCA and escalation deliverable) — agree.

If you approve the above, I will send the term-sheet and updated SOW to Rafael and procurement and route the PO acceptance path. If we need to push further on platform fee, we should ask for an accelerated payment milestone (50% at PO, 50% at production go-live) or a minimum monthly minimum that phases in.

Can you call out finance implications and whether Sean will sign off on the $50k fee and 120 hours?

Thanks,
Olga
